title: Denchūka
description: A concrete utility pole seen from directly beneath it, its transformers and crossarms standing in the sun against a summer sky and a towering cumulus rising behind the shaft, run forward through Japan's slow programme of burying its overhead lines. Drag sideways through the years. The wires go first: each one loses its tension, bows, and drops out of the sky along the converging verticals. Then the hardware is lowered down the pole, the lower transformers first and the crossarms last, and then the pole itself sinks along its own axis into the ground below the frame. The sky behind it is left clean, the cumulus standing in it. Drag back and it all comes back the way it went.
intent: Reality pieces: take a real photograph apart element by element and remove each piece together with its effects. Fourteen wires (sky matte with sub-pixel alpha; Hough segments grown into whole spans, and the bundle that runs up out of the top of the frame), the hardware in three pieces (SAM 2.1 for the transformers, the rest of the pole head given to the nearest), and the shaft (a cone fitted to SAM 2.1's mask) each become their own element; three clean plates are filled (a membrane of the sky round each hole, the bare shaft rebuilt from its own clean run below the hardware with a rounded end), so every in-between year is two neighbouring clean plates; moving pieces are unmixed against the plate behind them so they carry no sky. The sky is regraded live to a summer cobalt that deepens with elevation, and a real towering cumulus (an HDRI's convective tower, matted from its sky by its blue excess, unmixed, placed under the photograph's camera so its verticals converge on the zenith with the pole's) is laid into that same regrade through the same sky matte, so every removal uncovers more of it. Gravity is the camera's: MoGe-2's normals over the pole are all horizontal, so the direction they leave out is up; snapped onto the pole's axis it puts the camera about 55 degrees up and the zenith's vanishing point above the frame, and everything falls away from it. Reference: Japan's Act on the Promotion of Non-Utility-Pole Policies (無電柱化の推進に関する法律, 2016) and the MLIT programme, https://www.mlit.go.jp/road/road/traffic/chicyuka/ ; Japan has more than 35 million poles and still adds about 70,000 a year, https://www.japantimes.co.jp/opinion/2019/10/12/editorials/expedite-burying-power-cables
sources: Photograph: a pole with many wires and a sky background by ky kim (@kk0mtl) on Unsplash, Unsplash License. https://unsplash.com/photos/a-pole-with-many-wires-and-a-sky-background-0Ha29alvPK0 (file: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1702309400099-9e2712aca350, downloaded at 4000x2251). Cropped to 3:2 against its right edge and resampled to 2400x1600. Taken apart by tools/depth/bakes/denchuka (prep.py, masks.py, plates.py, export.py, solid.py for the concrete's clean edge; bird.py hands the bird sitting across one wire to that wire) with tools/depth depth_hr.py (Depth Anything V2 Small, Apache-2.0), segment.py (SAM 2.1 Hiera-Tiny, Apache-2.0; sky matte) and normals.py (MoGe-2 ViT-S, MIT).

Cloud: HDRI 'Skidpan', Poly Haven, by Dimitrios Savva (photography) and Jarod Guest (processing), CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/skidpan (16k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/16k%2B/skidpan_16k.hdr). Its towering cumulus (u 0.163, crown 27.6 deg up) matted from the sky by a soft blue-excess alpha (never eroded), unmixed from the fitted sky behind it and laid over the regraded cobalt, power lines filled, and placed in a vertical plane through the photograph's zenith at 2 times its angles (about 0.72 HDRI pixel to a plate pixel, near the photograph's own sharpness), turned 4 degrees, crown at plate (1350, 500) up behind the transformers, so the tower fills the right half of the frame and the dark pole cuts across it; the eucalyptus in front of its foot in the HDRI is replaced with the tower's own tree-free right flank, shifted across at the same elevation and matched in light, so the HDRI's ground stays below the frame; its anvil's flat shelf dissolved up from its base into the blue and its edge feathered (widest on the anvil), a pocket of the HDRI's sky in its foot filled, and its relief lifted and written from linear radiance as its light (deepest shade pocket to brightest crown, across all 8 bits) into cloud.webp and sky.png B by tools/depth/bakes/denchuka/cloud.py; graded live to luminous warm-neutral crowns (~0.92-0.97, the top percent or two rolled off under white) stepping down into saturated skylight-blue shade pockets (hue ~205, value ~0.70).
